PLEASE READ CAREFULLY before attempting this test!

Do NOT attempt to do this assessment on a mobile device or on the Pulse App - it will not work properly! Please access this test via eips.brightspace.com using a chromebook, laptop, or some sort of PC.

This is a closed book test. The only accessible resources available to you during the test is the Biology 30 Datasheet, which you should print off before starting, and a calculator.

Accessing your notes, the textbook, the internet (Google), emails, texts, Snap Chat, Tik Tok, Twitter (Etc...), or a friend or family member at ANY TIME DURING this assessment is considered CHEATING. If caught, you will be assigned a ZERO for this assessment, your principal will be contacted and a meeting will be required to determine if you will be given an opportunity to continue in the course. PLEASE consider having an adult supervise you if you think you may be tempted!

You will have only 1 attempt to do this unit test, so do not start it until you are absolutely ready. Once it is started you will have four hours to complete it. Any responses after the time is up will not be recorded.

Be sure everything is saved and SUBMITTED before the time is up!!

You will see 1 question per page. On this test there are 39 Multiple Choice questions, 6 Numeric Response questions, and 8 Written Response questions. Please plan your time accordingly.

 

Read over the following documents before attempting this test!:

How to attach images to written response

How to use the built-in Equation Editor in written response questions

 

Good luck!

Summarize the main features of incomplete dominance, multiple alleles, and codominance. Provide at least one example of each.

Incomplete dominance results when two alleles for a gene are equally dominant. When both are present, they produce an offspring whose phenotype is a mixture of both genes – a novel phenotype. (Possible example: Red and White make Pink)

Multiple alleles are a condition in which genes exist in more than two allelic forms. Each allele is expressed equally, and there is no intermediate or mixing of the expression of the alleles. (Possible example: Blood Type with IA, IB, and i alleles)

Codominance results when two alleles for a gene are equally dominant and the expression of each allele can be seen in the heterozygous condition. (Possible example: Roan horse with both black and white hairs present)

A tomato farmer has acquired a purple stemmed red tomato producing organism of unknown genotype. The farmer believes that if he crosses this tomato plant with an individual from the Punnet square you created in the previous question (the F1 generation), he will be able to determine the unknown genotype of his new acquisition. Identify the genotype of the F1 tomato plant that the farmer should use. Explain your selection.

Genotype of F1 that farmer should use  pptt.

The above mentioned F1 organism is homozygous recessive for both traits fitting the criteria for its use in a test cross. The acquired organism with unknown genotype shows the dominant phenotype for both traits yet it is unknown if he is heterozygous for one of both of the traits or homozygous dominant. By performing the test cross with the homozygous recessive individual from the F1 (pptt) the farmer will be able to determine the unknown genotype:

P_R_ X pprr

- if offspring are all purple stem and all Red tomato -> unknown genotype is PPRR

- if offspring are all purple stem and half Red tomato -> PPRr

- if offspring are half purple stem and all Red tomato -> PpRR

- if offspring are half purple stem and half Red tomato -> PpRr

Describe one piece of evidence obtained from the analysis of a pedigree chart that could be used to determine whether the mode of inheritance of a human genetic disorder is X-linked or autosomal (1 mark) AND one piece of evidence that could be used to determine whether it is recessive or dominant (1 mark).

X-linked - a greater number of males than females have the disorder, the disorder appears to be inherited from the mothers (maternal) side of the family.

Autosomal – the number of males and females with the disorder is roughly equal, the disorder appears to be inherited from either parent equally

 

Recessive – two parents without the disorder have a child with the disorder, the disorder skips a generation

Dominant – two parents with the disorder have a child without the disorder, the disorder is present in each generation or disappears from successive generations

Using a Punnett square, predict the probability of individuals III-11 and III-12’s next child being a male with CH. Explain why more females than males inherit CH in generation III. 

Genotypes (4 marks)

Allele Key (1 mark)

Predicted Probability (1 mark)

Explanation (2 marks)

Genotypes:                                            Allele Key:
II-4: XCY               IV-6: XCXc               XC–CH
II-5: XcXc              IV-7: XcY                 Xc–normal
III-11: XcY             IV-8: XCXc
III-12: XCXc          IV-9: XcXc

Punnett Square:

• Probability of III-11 and III-12’s child being male with CH (male with CH) XCY = 1/4 or 25%

• More females than males inherit CH in generation III because individual II-4, a male, has CH and because CH is X-linked dominant the father’s XC will be passed on to all his female children in generation III (but not to his sons who received the father’s Y chromosome).
